title: Eggs Royale: Smoked Salmon and Poached Eggs with Lemon Hollandaise
summary: Toasted English muffins are layered with smoked salmon and poached eggs with fully set yolks, then coated with a lemon hollandaise cooked over water to a safe 71 °C.
equipment: saucepan that the bowl sits on without touching the water
deep frying pan or wide saucepan (about 28 cm)

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, melted and kept warm

steps.title: Cook the yolks
steps.text: Put 3 cm water in the saucepan and bring it to a bare simmer. Whisk the yolks, lemon juice and water in the bowl, set it over the pan and whisk constantly for 3-5 minutes until thick, pale and leaving a trail, and the mixture reads 71 °C. If the edges start to look grainy, lift the bowl off for a few seconds; gentle, even heat thickens the yolks without scrambling them.

steps.title: Whisk in the butter
steps.text: Take the bowl off the heat and whisk in the warm butter a spoonful at a time, then in a thin stream, until the sauce is thick and glossy. Season with the cayenne and salt, and whisk in 1 tsp warm water if it is too thick. Keep it over the pan, off the heat, and use within 30 minutes.

steps.title: Drain the eggs
steps.text: Crack each egg into the sieve over a bowl and swirl for 20-30 seconds so the thin white drips away, then tip it into a ramekin. This gives neat, compact poached eggs.

steps.title: Poach in two batches
steps.text: Bring the water to the boil in the deep pan, then lower it to a bare simmer. Tip in 4 eggs, spaced apart, and cook for 6-7 minutes until the whites are firm and the yolks feel set when pressed (71 °C). Lift them into the bowl of hot water to keep warm and poach the other 4.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Toast the muffins and put 2 halves on each plate. Top with the smoked salmon, then a drained egg, blotted on kitchen paper. Spoon over the hollandaise, scatter with dill and serve straight away.

tips: If the hollandaise starts to split, whisk a spoonful of warm water into a clean bowl and slowly whisk the sauce back into it.
Do not let the bowl touch the water; direct heat scrambles the yolks.
Make the sauce first and keep it warm off the heat, so you can concentrate on the eggs.
Blot the eggs well, or their water will thin the sauce.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Hollandaise does not keep; leftover salmon and muffins can be refrigerated separately for up to 2 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
